description: The first pass contains 32 English, Arabic and French open-web queries across broad news, weekly/rights, labor/sector, regions, early-month and boundary searches, and 63 source cards. Some batches returned pooled URLs without result totals or per-query URL attribution. Syndicated/republished reports are scoped to credited sources and not counted as independent confirmation automatically. This is documented open-web coverage, not exhaustive or LexisNexis-equivalent.
required_followup: Continue bounded multilingual searches for early, sector and regional actions; preserve empty/relevant returns and source chains; do not claim absence/exhaustiveness.

description: HRW and Al Jazeera support Jan25 as the onset of the Tripoli sequence, but consecutive-day labels conflict. Physical end after Jan28 is unknown; Jan31 follows a described lull and may be a resumption. Jan3/12/15/23 Tripoli actions have distinct or incomplete chronology, with no proved continuous physical occupation.
required_followup: Apply current Coding Procedure when available to nightly units and Jan31 resumption; establish physical starts/ends. Do not transfer counts across nights.

description: Opened reports confirm separate actions Jan23/25 in Saida, Beirut, Beddawi-area and Tripoli, plus a Jan28 Beirut march; most lack concurrent crowd estimates. Chtoura, Nabatieh and Saifi remain search-only. About ten at Baalbek Jan31 is excluded. Other South/Bekaa roadblocks are not sufficiently localized for separate event records.
required_followup: Seek local attendance and demand evidence; clarify shared locations and multi-location reports; do not treat injuries, arrests, vehicles, blocked roads or calls as attendance/execution.

description: One death, Omar Tayba, is reported after Jan27 clashes. Amnesty relays his brother’s ISF-fire/ricochet account; HRW reviews footage linking ISF fire and a person falling but also records the commander’s unidentified-bullet explanation. Al Jazeera relayed a mayoral second-death claim; L’Orient Today corrected it and said Osama Ghoumrawy was alive and uninjured. Code one reported death only. Injuries do not establish crowd size.
required_followup: Retain source attribution and official counter-account; keep death/injury dates distinct and review any later primary reporting.

description: Opened LBCI confirms Jan3 Tripoli processions over living conditions/prices but no crowd count; Jan12 taxi drivers protested a lockdown work ban without a count. Jan23 sources describe separate Saida, Beddawi-area and Tripoli actions, also uncounted. Jan15 Tripoli and Chtoura/Nabatieh/Saifi leads remain search-only or incomplete. Teacher/contract-worker searches found calls, suspensions and remote/open strike notices, not a verified 50-person in-person assembly. A broad statement about protests since Jan14 gives no specific event date/count. No continuity is established across gaps.
required_followup: Continue coverage for early-month and sector actions, verifying actual gatherings/dates/attendance; distinguish strikes, road disruption and public assemblies.

description: Amnesty’s 35 arrests cover Jan25–31 and include people taken from homes or summoned; HRW’s later detainee report covers post-event detention/torture; Al Jazeera Feb1 reports detainees/injuries over recent days. Do not assign these totals to Jan31 or a specific night. Silence remains unknown.
required_followup: Seek date-specific reporting; separate street arrests from home raids/summonses and later treatment; distinguish live rounds from gas/rubber.

description: The Fahmi-home “nearly 100” estimate appears under CLDH’s Jan29 heading while its embedded Daily Star URL is dated Jan28; L’Orient Today’s opened Jan28 report confirms the march without a count. The Daily Star page itself was not opened. Some L’Orient Today text remains subscriber-gated; its stale two-deaths headline does not override the body correction. Jan3/Jan15 OLJ articles remain search-only after cache misses; the worker’s ordinary HTTPS attempts failed at DNS, while the coordinator independently received HTTP 403 from both same public URLs. Neither body/caption was opened and no barrier was bypassed.
required_followup: Respect partial/paywalled text and failed public access; do not bypass access controls. Retain the date/count conflict until a public source resolves it.
